text: Ingests raw content (conversations, documents, files, URLs) and automatically extracts memories from it
quote: Send any raw content to Supermemory — conversations, documents, files, URLs. We extract the memories automatically.

text: Hybrid search mode searches both memories and document chunks together for best relevance
quote: Use `searchMode: "hybrid"` for best results. It searches both memories and document chunks, returning the most relevant content.

text: Automatically maintains user profiles as collections of facts built from all their interactions, always ready without needing a search
quote: User profiles are **automatically maintained collections of facts about your users** that Supermemory builds from all their interactions.

text: Container tags act as hard namespace boundaries so a search scoped to one tag never returns another tag's memories
quote: A container tag is a hard boundary — its own namespace. Memories in one tag are never returned by a search scoped to another tag.

text: Provides a remote MCP server that lets an agent search Supermemory's documentation while implementing an integration
quote: Remote MCP that lets the agent search Supermemory documentation while it implements an integration.

text: Official CLI can detect a project and launch/print an integration setup flow
quote: npx supermemory setup # detect project, launch/print integration flow

text: Can run the memory engine on your own hardware as a single self-contained binary
quote: Supermemory runs on your own hardware. It's the same memory engine behind the hosted platform... as a single self-contained binary.

text: Fully local deployment mode with local graph engine, local embeddings, and local LLM so data never leaves your infrastructure
quote: Local graph engine, local embeddings, local LLM. Your data never leaves the building.

text: Ships a MemoryBench Claude Code skill that automates benchmarking a custom memory implementation against Supermemory, Mem0, and Zep
quote: MemoryBench ships a Claude Code skill that automates the entire process of benchmarking a custom memory implementation — yours — against Supermemory, Mem0, and Zep.

text: Can create memories directly without going through document ingestion; they are embedded and immediately searchable
quote: Create memories directly without going through the document ingestion workflow. Memories are embedded and immediately searchable.

text: Connectors for Google Drive, Gmail, Notion, OneDrive, and GitHub auto-sync content via real-time webhooks
quote: Connectors Google Drive · Gmail · Notion · OneDrive · GitHub — auto-sync with real-time webhooks.

text: Supermemory MCP gives every MCP-compatible assistant a shared memory layer so multiple tools use the same authorized context
quote: Supermemory MCP gives every MCP-compatible assistant a shared memory layer, so technical and non-technical teams can collaborate with AI using the same authorized context.

text: Each end-user/tenant can be scoped to a container tag, and that container's content can be deleted on request to satisfy deletion requests
quote: Scope each end-user (or tenant) to a container tag. When the user requests deletion, delete that container's content via the API / console workf

text: Only unique ingested content is billed; repeated content costs nothing via a built-in prompt-cache discount
quote: only unique content we ingest is billed; repeats cost nothing (100% prompt-cache discount, baked in).

text: Builds a living knowledge graph of facts layered on other facts, rather than a static store of embeddings
quote: Supermemory builds a living knowledge graph of facts on top of other facts — not a static folder of embeddings

text: Provides an official agent skill so the agent uses real endpoints, auth, and containerTag rules instead of hallucinating APIs
quote: Install the official skill so the agent uses the real endpoints, auth, and `containerTag` rules instead of hallucinating APIs

text: Retrieval can be done three ways: document search (RAG), memory graph traversal, and user profile lookup
quote: Retrieve three ways — document search (RAG), memory graph traversal, and user profile

text: Official client SDKs available for TypeScript (npm) and Python (pip)
quote: Official clients wrap this API: TypeScript: npm install supermemory Python: pip install supermemory

text: Search API supports an includeRelatedMemories option to traverse related memories/graph connections
quote: const results = await client.search({ q: "where does Alex work?", containerTag: "user_123", include: { relatedMemories: true }, });

text: Memories can be flagged isStatic for permanent identity traits, while other memories default to non-static (decaying) behavior
quote: isStatic: true for permanent identity traits (name, hometown). Defaults to false

text: Using the same customId lets you update existing documents/conversations, reprocessing only what changed
quote: Use customId to update existing documents or conversations. When you send content with the same customId, Supermemory intelligently processes only what's new.

text: Self-hosted binary requires no Docker, no database provisioning, and no config files — boots in seconds
quote: No Docker. No database to provision. No config files. It boots in seconds with everything built in

text: Users can interact via natural language and the assistant automatically selects the right Supermemory tool, no code or tool names needed
quote: Ask naturally. The assistant selects the right Supermemory tool without requiring code or tool names.

text: Spaces keep a team's documents, memories, and profile context focused so retrieval doesn't mix unrelated work
quote: A space keeps a team's documents, memories, and profile context focused, so AI retrieves the right knowledge without mixing unrelated work.

text: Multi-modal extractors handle PDFs, images (OCR), videos (transcription), and code (AST-aware chunking) automatically on upload
quote: Multi-modal Extractors | PDFs, images (OCR), videos (transcription), code (AST-aware chunking). Upload and it works.

text: MemoryBench can be run yourself against your own memory implementation on datasets matching your use case
quote: you can run it yourself, against your own memory implementation, on the datasets that match your use case

text: app.supermemory.ai is a separate consumer product built on the same engine, distinct from where API keys are issued
quote: app.supermemory.ai is the consumer product on the same engine — not where you mint API keys.
